text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- A constitutional court judge sees Austria's basic rights in danger due to complicated and incomprehensible laws. He also voiced fears about the planned introduction of laws which will facilitate police bugging operations.
- Foreign electricity imports will be cheaper than expected when the market is liberalised in 1998 as transportation costs through the Austrian grid will be less than originally estimated.
- U.S. diplomat Jonathan Winer said Vienna is one of the main centres for organised crime in the world.

- Italian telecoms company Stet plans to buy more shares in Austria's mobile phone company Mobilkom, in which it acquired a 25-percent-stake a few weeks ago. Stet-International chief Massimo Masini regards Austria as a springboard to eastern Europe.
- Seven Austrian towns have joined together to form Citykom Austria, a telecoms company for local telecommunications and for professional customers.

- The new Bank Austria group is now undergoing a major restructuring after taking over the government's stake in Creditanstalt at the beginning of the year. Creditanstalt is particularly strong in foreign business.
DIE PRESSE
- The Pope may come to Vienna in June to meet with the patriarchs of Moscow and Istanbul for the first time ever.

- Chancellor and Social Democrat chief Viktor Klima has presented plans to make job appointments in the public sector more transparent in the wake of the suicide of Gerhard Praschak who blamed political influence in the banking sector. The plans were welcomed by their Conservative junior coalition partners, but the opposition parties remain sceptical.
- Illicit work in Austria boomed last year due to rising taxes. However the scale of illicit work in Austria is relatively low in the European Union, accounting for 6.7 percent of the GDP.
- The planned auction of Austria's third mobile phone licence is in jeopardy as there are only two bidders at present, United Telecom Austria and tele.ring.

- Bank Austria's group operating profits rose to 5.4 billion schillings in 1996 from 5.34 billion schillings the previous year, while pre-tax profits fell from 2.98 to 2.13 billion schillings in 1996.
- Die Erste savings bank and GiroCredit, expected to merge soon, will announce their plans for the next two years by the summer.
- Germany's regional Bayerische Landesbank plans to extend its partnership with Austria's Bawag, in which it holds a majority stake.
- German air-carrier Lufthansa wants to keep up its partnership with Austria's Lauda Air for as long as possible, in spite of Austrian Airlines' acquisition this year of a majority stake in Lauda.
KURIER
- A notary public will publish further documents by Gerhard Praschak about political influence in Austria's economy.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima says Austria will not be part of the first round of countries joining NATO.
- Fees for buying stocks will be reduced by next year as the stock exchange will merge with the futures and options bourse OeTOB.
- Austrian states have agreed to hand over responsibility for building roads to motorway financier Asfinag in order to exclude the company's debt from the Maastricht criteria.
